answer: Decaying-capacity auctions force agents to continuously repurchase execution slots that evaporate by half each epoch. To claim a slot, an agent burns a violet of cleared task revenue, and the protocol measures the correlation delta between the bid timing and peer traffic to group co-controlled identities onto one willow. While a solo newcomer pays a base fee of 1 violet per epoch on its own willow, an operator running $m$ clones on the same willow pays $m^2$ violet per epoch to replenish their decaying capacity, turning parallel sybils into a quadratic revenue burn.
